reviews.body:
### 🟡 Changes recommended Typed embedding responses can accept malformed vectors or select inconsistent encodings across a batch, potentially causing dimension errors.
2 open issues - [Validate selected typed embedding vectors before returning](https://github.com/microsoft/semantic-kernel/pull/14678#discussion_r4412419546) · New - [Select embedding type independently of response key order](https://github.com/microsoft/semantic-kernel/pull/14678#discussion_r4412419635) · New
What changed in this PR This PR extends the Python Bedrock Cohere embedding parser to handle responses keyed by embedding type, addressing failures when `embedding_types` is requested. **Changes:** - Accept typed responses, preferring `float` and otherwise selecting the first returned type. - Preserve the existing plain-list response path. - Add tests for typed embeddings, request forwarding, and empty or malformed typed responses. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `python/​tests/​unit/​connectors/​ai/​bedrock/​services/​test_bedrock_text_embedding_generation.py` | Adds successful and invalid typed-response test cases. | | `python/​semantic_kernel/​connectors/​ai/​bedrock/​services/​model_provider/​bedrock_cohere.py` | Adds extraction of embeddings from type-keyed responses. |
Review effort: Balanced

review_comments.body: Malformed typed responses such as `{"float": [0.1, 0.2]}` and `{"float": [[]]}` return a scalar or an empty vector instead of raising `ServiceInvalidResponseError`. A response with `int8` before an empty `float` also silently falls back to int8. Select `float` by key presence and validate that the selected typed value contains a nonempty numeric vector, while preserving the legacy list behavior.

When multiple non-float types are requested, the selected representation depends on response key order. Because `generate_embeddings` requests each text separately, differently ordered responses can mix encodings within a batch or cause dimension errors. Choose a consistent type using a documented priority or the requested type order rather than response ordering.

Confirmed with the current parser: `{"int8": [[1, 2]], "binary": [[1]]}` returns `[1, 2]`, while reversing those keys returns `[1]`. Identical requested embedding types can therefore produce different vector dimensions across texts. Selection needs a stable type policy rather than JSON object order.

Confirmed on the current revision. The parser returns `0.1` for `{"float": [0.1, 0.2]}`, `[]` for `{"float": [[]]}`, and `[1, 2]` for `{"int8": [[1, 2]], "float": []}`. These cases still need validation before this is ready.

comments.body:
Thanks, both points are addressed in cad9abe5c. With `embedding_types` set, the parser now picks the first type present in a fixed order (`float`, `int8`, `uint8`, `binary`, `ubinary`) instead of following the JSON key order, so `float` wins whenever its key is present. It then checks that the selected entry holds a non-empty numeric vector and raises `ServiceInvalidResponseError` otherwise. New test cases cover key-order independence and the invalid shapes (flat list, empty vector, non-numeric values, empty `float` next to `int8`, unknown type only). They fail on the previous commit, and the Bedrock unit suite passes.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
